idea: H^5 with coordinate-shift orbit (order 5), H = D7 (|G| = 537,824), plus free random S on the same G
valid: none: no S reaches diameter 12; checker not run (no cost-0 candidate)
finding: NEGATIVE, structural: G/[G,G] = (Z2)^5 needs 5 generators, but Haar connectivity needs <s^-1 t : s,t in S> = G, and 5 elements give differences of rank <= 4 in Z2^5 (exhaustive over the 5-set model: rank 4 max). Measured: every random 5-set and 22 orbit samples reach only N or N/2 (or N/4) of the 2N vertices from (e,A); costs 1.075M to 1.086M; orbit-closed S (cyclic shifts of sign vectors) have rank 4 in 187,484 of 200,000 samples. Any shift-invariant S has constant coordinate-sign sum, so H^5 shift families need H perfect (A5^5 is too big).
next: Dead for Delta=5 in H^5 form: try order-5 automorphisms acting on G/G' as the F16 component (rank-4 module, no fixed vector), e.g. C7^4 x| Z2^4 with a zeta_5 action, which keeps G/G' rank 4 and avoids the sum invariant.

valid: none (no cost-0 S; BFS criterion only, apsp not needed)
finding: Only nonabelian H with |H|^3 in [35089,40000] is D17 (33 is cyclic only: no nonabelian group of order 33). Every D17^3 orbit S is disconnected unless x has weight-1 reflection pattern; the 4,913 such orbits all reach only ~11.6k of 39.3k B-vertices (B-unreached 27,707, A-unreached 21,670, best 49,377, nearly identical for all orbits). next: H^3 shift family is dead in the 35k-40k window (abelian normal subgroup wall); try groups with no large abelian normal subgroup and N ~ 35k, or drop the cube structure.
